$comment: Command classification for the Cratis PreToolUse Bash guard (cratis-guard-store-mutations.sh).
Data, not code: a consuming repository extends or replaces this without touching the script.
- drop a cratis-store-mutations.local.json next to this file to ADD entries (merged, never replaces)
- or point CRATIS_HOOKS_STORE_MUTATIONS at a replacement file
A command listed in "mutating" is blocked even when a local file also lists it in "readOnly", so a
local file can tighten the shipped lists but only a replacement file can loosen them.
Scope: only the "group" command group is guarded. Every other cratis group (ai, arc, context, llm,
screenplay, prologue, completions) and every top-level command (init, new, render, run, update,
version, get-started, llm-context) is out of scope and always allowed.
Fields:
verifiedAgainst  the cratis CLI version whose `cratis llm-context` these lists were derived from
group            the guarded command group
helpOptions      options that print help instead of running; allowed wherever they appear
versionOptions   options that print the version instead of running a command; allowed wherever they appear
flagOptions      global/group options that take no value, skipped while reading the command path
valueOptions     global/group options that take a value, skipped with that value
readOnly         the allowlist: command paths below the group that only read state
command  the command path, space-separated, e.g. "observers list"
reason   why it is safe to run without a human's authorization
mutating         known command paths that change server, client or external state
command  the command path
effect   what it changes; shown to the agent in the block message
Anything under the group that is on neither list is blocked as unknown: the guard fails closed, so a
command added by a newer CLI is refused until someone classifies it here.

readOnly.reason: runs a health check and returns a diagnostic report
shows the cached token's expiry and identity
shows one event type registration and its schema
reads events from an event sequence
returns the highest used sequence number
shows one failed partition and its error
lists namespaces in an event store
lists a read model's replay history
reads snapshots of one read model instance

mutating.effect: replays an observer from the beginning of the event log, resetting all state it has built
replays one partition of an observer from the beginning, resetting that partition's state
retries a failed partition from the sequence number where it failed
clears an observer's quarantine so it resumes processing
resumes a stopped or failed background job
executes a server recommendation, such as a schema or replay maintenance action
marks a recommendation as ignored so it no longer appears
adds an event store subscription to a target event store
removes an event store subscription from a target event store
adds a user to the server's user store
removes a user from the server
registers an application with the server
removes an application registration from the server
authenticates with a username and password and caches a token that later commands use
opens a pre-filled GitHub issue in the browser
opens the interactive terminal Workbench, whose keys replay observers and retry or replay failed partitions; only a human at a terminal can drive it
